newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev inches up to 1,569-1,572 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev inches up to 1,569-1,572 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev edged up to 1,569-1,572 per dollar at 0800 GMT from the opening 1,570-1,574 against the background of a rise in the central bank main interest rate, dealers said.
"Banks and clients are selling dollars for levs to place bids at the government securities auctions, while there are very few bidders," a commercial bank dealer said.
The higher main rate was expected to boost yields on floating interest T-bills and increase investor interest.
A rise in the central bank main interest rate to 48.72 percent annually from 43.08 percent took effect on Monday.

The Finance Ministry offers 20 billion lev worth of floating interest T-bills with maturities of six, nine and 12 months, 11 billion levs of three-month discount T-bills and 24 billion levs of four-week discount paper at auctions on Monday.
The yield of the floating interest T-bills is set equal to the main rate until maturity and varies with each change in the main rate.
Traders reported low lev liquidity in banks amid the increased foreign currency supply.
"The lack of large receipts from treasury paper investments today has impaired banks' lev liquidity," another dealer said.

Traders however were cautious in unloading dollar positions across the board due to uncertainty to which anchor currency and at what exchange rate the lev would be pegged under a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to stabilise the economy.

"If the lev is pegged at 1,000 per mark today, this should give around 1710 levs per dollar under the current dollar/mark exchange rate on international markets, yielding around 140 levs in the month ahead," a third dealer said.
Bulgaria's Finance Minister Muravei Radev said last week that a lev/dollar exchange rate of 1,600 or 1,000 levs to the German mark was assumed in this year's budget draft.
The government has pledged to introduce the system on July 1. The anchor currency and the exact exchange rate are to be approved by parliament by then.

Today's trade was seen around 1,570 levs per dollar and the central bank was was expected to bid for dollars around this level to halt a lev rise and boost its reserves ahead of the implementation of the currency board system, dealers said.
Under the currency board system levs in circulation should be exactly matched by central bank foreign exchange reserves. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
